https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/tate-brothers-.text: Just months after returning to the United States with vocal support from figures in Donald Trump's political circle, Andrew and Tristan Tate have been arrested by US Marshals on a British extradition request and now face dozens of criminal charges in the UK.The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has authorised a series of additional charges against the brothers, including new counts of rape, trafficking and sexual offences, bringing the total number of alleged victims in the UK case to seven.Andrew Tate, 39, has been charged with seven further counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm, and 19 further offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.Tristan Tate, 38, faces two further counts of rape, one count of sexual assault and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation. The alleged offences are said to have taken place between July 2010 and August 2017.From MAGA Backing to ArrestThe arrests mark a dramatic shift for the brothers, who were allowed to leave Romania earlier this year after spending more than two years under travel restrictions while facing separate criminal proceedings there.During that time, several high-profile figures aligned with Donald Trump publicly questioned the Romanian case. Donald Trump Jr described Andrew Tate's detention as 'absolute insanity', while Romanian Foreign Minister Emil Hurezeanu said a Trump administration envoy raised the brothers' case during the Munich Security Conference.Although there is no evidence the Trump administration secured their release, the Tate brothers' return to Florida fuelled speculation that they had gained influential supporters within Trump's political movement.That perception is now being tested after US Marshals arrested the brothers on behalf of UK authorities.UK Widens Criminal CaseThe latest charges bring the total number Andrew Tate faces in the UK to 42, including allegations of rape, human trafficking, assault and offences relating to indecent images of a child. Tristan Tate now faces 17 charges, including rape, sexual assault and trafficking-related offences.Malcolm McHaffie, Head of the CPS Special Crime Division, said the new charging decisions followed a further file of evidence from Bedfordshire Police and increased the number of alleged victims to seven.He also reminded the public that both defendants are entitled to a fair trial and urged people not to publish material that could prejudice the proceedings.Extradition Proceedings BeginThe brothers were arrested by the US Marshals Service in Miami on 18 July following the UK's extradition request. The Department of Justice confirmed the arrests were made under existing extradition treaties between the United States and the United Kingdom.The Tate brothers are expected to appear before a federal court in Miami as extradition proceedings begin.Their lawyer, Joseph McBride, said they deny all allegations and argued the UK should not seek extradition while separate criminal proceedings in Romania remain ongoing.Andrew and Tristan Tate, who hold dual British and American citizenship, also face criminal proceedings in Romania over allegations of human trafficking and sexually exploiting women. They deny all wrongdoing in both Romania and the UK.

https://www.politico.eu/article/vladimir.text: Authorities in Tokyo lashed out at Moscow after a visit by Russian President Vladimir Putin to the disputed island of Iturup on Thursday. The island, also known by its Japanese name Etorofu, lies northeast of Japan — around 100 kilometers from the coast of Hokkaido — in the Kuril Islands chain and is claimed by both Moscow and Tokyo. Like the other disputed islands in the chain, they are administered by Russia. Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi wrote on X on Thursday: “Today, I was informed that Russian President Putin visited Iturup Island. The Northern Territories, including Iturup Island, are inherently Japanese territory both historically and under international law, and the Government of Japan strongly protests this visit.” Advertisement Advertisement Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called the visit “incompatible with Japan’s consistent position on the Northern Territories” and “absolutely unacceptable.” “Even amid the harsh state of Japan-Russia relations following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Japan has made every possible effort,” wrote Takaichi on X, “but this visit can only be said to have further hardened anti-Russia sentiment within Japan and made medium- to long-term recovery of relations more difficult. I hope that the Russian side will take the gravity of this matter very seriously.” Moscow, however, claims the island chain became part of Russian territory following Japan’s defeat in World War II. The Kremlin also operates a strategically important military base on Iturup. In 2025, Japan protested a Russian shooting drill in waters in the area, including in Japan’s territorial waters, and said that the Kremlin’s “military buildup” in the area was “unacceptable.” According to Russian state media , Putin visited a fish farm on the island. The report said that he was told that the waters of the Kuril Islands are currently filled with tuna weighing up to 300 kilograms — and he was also treated to caviar. This story has been updated. https://telex.hu/transtelex/2026/08/25/n.text: Menü Kereső Az Orbán-kritikus EP-alelnök Magyar Péternél lobbizna az erdélyi támogatásokért Transtelex frissítve Tőkés Hunor (Transtelex) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Ștefănuță szerint több erdélyi szervezettől olyan jelzést kapott, hogy késnek a támogatások, vagy bizonytalanná vált a finanszírozásuk, egyes rendezvényeket pedig emiatt el kellett halasztani vagy fel kellett függeszteni, írja a politikus a kedden kiadott közleményében . Konkrét szervezeteket vagy rendezvényeket nem nevezett meg. A független romániai EP-képviselő levelet is írt a miniszterelnöknek és Tarr Zoltánnak, amelyben találkozót kezdeményezett a magyar állami támogatások ügyének megtárgyalása érdekében. Azt írta, kész személyesen Budapestre utazni, és amellett érvelt, hogy a fesztiválokat, gyerek- és ifjúsági táborokat, valamint más kulturális programokat szervező közösségeket nem a politikai kötődésük, hanem a munkájuk alapján kellene megítélni. Ștefănuță a román kormánytól is segítséget kérne, többek között a kulturális minisztériumhoz fordulna. Szerinte Romániának és Magyarországnak egyaránt érdeke, hogy az erdélyi magyar kulturális projektek átlátható és kiszámítható finanszírozáshoz jussanak. Erdélyi román politikusként úgy fogalmazott, a romániai magyar közösség képviseletét is feladatának tekinti. A megkeresés azért is aktuális, mert a tavasszal hivatalba lépett Tisza-kormány éppen átvilágítja és átalakítja az előző kormány külhoni támogatási rendszerét. Tarr Zoltán júliusi erdélyi útján arról beszélt , hogy felszámolnák azt a rendszert, amelyben szerinte a pénzek egy része politikai lojalitáshoz és informális kapcsolatokhoz kötődött. A kormány az elmúlt tíz év nagyobb külhoni támogatásainak felhasználását is vizsgálja. A Tisza-kormány ugyanakkor azt állítja, hogy nem a határon túli magyar támogatások megszüntetésére készül. Heidl György társadalmi kapcsolatokért felelős államtitkár néhány napja arról beszélt a Transtelexen is bemutatott interjúban , hogy növelnék a nyílt pályázatok arányát, a hosszú távon működő intézményeknek pedig kiszámíthatóbb finanszírozást adnának. A kormány nyilvánossá tenné a Bethlen Gábor Alap részletes támogatási adatbázisát is. Ștefănuță az országgyűlési választások előtt élesen kritizálta Orbán Viktort. Márciusban az Európai Parlamentben arra biztatta az erdélyi és anyaországi magyarokat, hogy menjenek el szavazni és válasszák a politikai változást, mert Orbán képzelt ellenségképek gyártásával igyekszik elterelni a figyelmet a gazdasági lecsúszásról, az inflációról és a lepusztult kórházakról. A felszólalás akkora hullámokat vert, hogy Orbán Viktor az X-en ment neki a zöldpárti alelnöknek, kioktatást emlegetve, amire Ștefănuță három nyelven vágott vissza azzal, hogy „a magyarok jobbat érdemelnek”. Ștefănuță később a Transtelexnek adott interjúban azt is elmondta, meglepte, hogy a magyar miniszterelnök időt szánt arra, hogy vele vitatkozzon. Azt is állította, hogy erdélyi magyar civil szervezetektől olyan panaszokat hallott, amelyek szerint az Orbán-kormány a támogatásokért politikai lojalitást várt el. Ștefănuță 2025-ben az Európai Parlament budapesti Pride-ra érkező delegációját is vezette, és többször nyilvánosan bírálta az Orbán-kormány politikáját. A mostani budapesti megkeresésével a román politikus arra tesz kísérletet, hogy a választási kampány utáni új politikai helyzetben közvetítőként lépjen fel az erdélyi magyar civil szféra és a budapesti döntéshozók között. https://www.budapesttimes.hu/world/stude.text: The Budapest Times Students falling behind neighbours as reading scores hit record low The 2025 PISA survey data from the OECD — the organisation comprising the world's most developed countries — which examines the practical competencies of 15-year-old students, points to a global crisis in education, the minister of education and children's affairs declared at a press conference presenting the survey's results. Judit Lannert stated that Hungary’s results in the survey, which focuses on mathematics, reading comprehension, and this time particularly on natural sciences, fall in line with this trend — and that Hungarian students are performing slightly below average, especially in the area of reading comprehension. According to the minister, it is cause for concern that Hungarian education appears to be falling behind even at a regional level, given that Czech, Polish, and Estonian students also performed better in the survey. She added that the proportion of top performers is also declining, which means that the institutional framework for nurturing talented students in Hungary needs to be reformed. She described it as a positive finding that, in the perception of Hungarian children, teachers pay more attention to them than teachers in other countries do to their students. She also noted that Hungarian students are above average in terms of discipline, and that this indicator has further improved over the past decade. Judit Lannert added that the survey also reveals that Hungarian parents are talking to their children about school less and less. For this reason, the ministry intends to set up a dedicated working group to engage with parents. He also described it as encouraging that Hungarian students perform particularly well in the area of environmental awareness. In Hungary, 86 percent of students believe they are capable of having a positive impact on the environment, which exceeds the OECD average of 81 percent. Some 67 percent of Hungarian students are interested in contributing to environmental protection through their future work, compared to an OECD average of just 62 percent. A serious problem, however — the minister continued — is that 5 percent of students have experienced online bullying, and one fifth have experienced other forms of bullying in the past 12 months, a trend that is increasing both in Hungary and across the OECD average. A professional working group at the ministry has therefore been set up to address the issue. According to Judit Lannert, the global decline in reading comprehension is driven by the growing use of digital devices at the expense of traditional reading. However, digital distraction is less pronounced in Hungary than the OECD average, which she attributed to the fact that mobile phone use is restricted in 90 percent of institutions. She added that the ministry is working on developing an AI strategy to ensure the appropriate use of artificial intelligence. In response to a question, the minister said that reading comprehension is to be improved through a new national core curriculum aimed at strengthening basic competencies. The development of the core curriculum is expected to take around a year and a half, she indicated. Kristóf Velkey, head of the public education analysis department at the Educational Authority, outlined that in 2025 a record number of 91 countries took part in the assessment, with approximately 6,400 students from 273 institutions in Hungary. The results are measured against the average of OECD member states, a figure that depends on how many countries belong to the organisation at the time of each assessment, which has been held every three years since 2000. The 2025 average will thus be derived from the measurements of 38 states, whereas when the assessments began the organisation had only 23 members, he explained. He noted at the outset that the international PISA results are now the lowest in all three assessed areas — mathematics, reading comprehension, and science — since the assessments began in 2000, with the Hungarian figures being particularly concerning with regard to reading comprehension. According to his statement, Hungarian students achieved an average score of 480 points in science, which does not differ significantly from the OECD average of 486 points. It is not significantly different from the results of Germany, Slovakia, or Croatia, for example, but is lower than the results of students in Austria, the Czech Republic, or Poland. The best results were recorded in the Chinese regions, Singapore, Taiwan, and Japan, while among European countries it was Estonian students who performed best, he listed. In reading comprehension — the head of department continued — Hungarian students scored 452 points, which is significantly below the OECD average of 461 points and comparable to the results of countries such as France, Croatia, Norway, and Slovakia. The top performers in this area are also Asian countries, while in Europe it is Irish and Estonian students who lead. In mathematics, however, the average score of Hungarian students is 459 points, which does not differ significantly from the OECD country average of 463 points, he added. Kristóf Velkey stated that compared to the previous 2022 results, the average score of participating countries fell by 14 points, and a significant decline of at least 20 points — in Hungary’s case, 21 points — was observed in 14 countries, including Hungary. Furthermore, mathematics results for Hungarian students were 9 points lower compared to the 2022 data. Only the science results — including Hungary’s — do not differ significantly from those of three years ago. He noted that with regard to reading comprehension, the OECD attributes the worsening trend to a decline in reading for pleasure and the growing prevalence of digital reading. The rapid scrolling of social media is endangering students’ ability to engage deeply with complex texts and data. He also spoke about how the PISA assessment — similarly to the organisations of the United Nations and the European Union — pays particular attention to underperforming students. The EU’s current target — which, according to the assessment, we are now moving away from — is for the proportion of underperforming students to fall below 15 percent by 2030. In their case, the risk is greatest that they will be left with gaps in the core competencies needed for further education and for successful integration into society and the labour market, said Kristóf Velkey. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text: Israeli troops destroy Hebron neighbourhood following attack on military checkpoint West Bank Israeli soldiers raze neighbourhood in Hebron, driving families from homes PM Benjamin Netanyahu vows ‘to destroy this place’ in retaliation for militant attack on army checkpoint Julian Borger in Jerusalem Sat 24 Oct 2026 09.17 EDT First published on Sat 24 Oct 2026 08.37 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Israeli troops have levelled a neighbourhood in Hebron, driving out hundreds of families in collective punishment for a militant attack on an army checkpoint outside the West Bank city, local Palestinian authorities said. The Hebron municipality estimated that 35 hectares (86 acres) had been destroyed or marked for destruction and about 1,500 people had been evicted from their homes by Saturday afternoon in the district of Ein Deir Baha. The whole city of 250,000 people was sealed off by checkpoints on every point of entry. Videos sent by a Hebron resident showed a substantial area of devastation with every house over several blocks flattened in an urban area. One video showed soldiers marking Palestinian houses with a sprayed black cross, another showed a bulldozer tearing down a stone wall on a hillside and another showed a large residential building festooned with Israeli flags. View image in fullscreen Soldiers patrol the northern checkpoint in Hebron after Israeli forces levelled a neighbourhood in Hebron. Photograph: John Wessels/AFP/Getty People said the building was the home of a prominent Hebron family that had been commandeered as a temporary military headquarters. The large-scale demolitions follow an attack on Friday on an Israeli military checkpoint outside Hebron by two gunmen. After a 20-minute gunfight, two Israeli soldiers were killed, three injured and the two gunmen were also killed. Israeli elections will take place in four days and the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu , and the extreme-right finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, travelled to the site of the attack to promise an immediate and ferocious response. View image in fullscreen Israel's finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, filmed himself wearing body armour in front of a Palestinian building being demolished. Photograph: Ammar Awad/Reuters Heidi Levine recounts how Palestinian youths helped save her in settler attack Read more Netanyahu said Israel would “act to destroy this place”. Smotrich who is standing for election in a smaller coalition party, had himself filmed wearing body armour in front of a Palestinian building being demolished. He said he had ordered “the immediate demolition of a wide row of illegal Arab structures adjacent to the attack site”. Smotrich also called for “a comprehensive military campaign … exactly like in Gaza and Lebanon”. Ein Deir Baha, the focus of the demolitions, was alleged to be the home district of the two gunmen. A spokesperson for the Hebron municipality said that about 300 families had been evicted. Some had taken refuge in the homes of friends and relatives, while the municipality said it had opened community halls and children’s play areas to shelter others. View image in fullscreen A Palestinian man clears debris outside a business demolished by Israeli forces in Hebron. Photograph: John Wessels/AFP/Getty A Palestinian news agency, Wafa, reported Israeli plans to displace a further 2,500 people. “We are being collectively punished for something we neither did nor supported,” a Hebron civil rights activist, Issa Amro, said. “Our suffering is being turned into political material for Israel’s elections, while innocent families pay the price.” Amro said his sister’s family was one of the hundreds driven out of their homes. “We are talking about hundreds of families who left their homes because of this, and they are not at all connected to what happened yesterday [Friday],” Amro said in a telephone interview. “It’s a very big area and we don’t know what’s going on, whether it is only election propaganda or if it’s a serious plan from decisions on what to do after the election.” The Israeli army was approached for comment on the operations and on videos showing extensive devastation.
